Note: What is often called Passover today has its origins in two ancient observances. Nissan 14 was the Passover as mentioned in the Torah; at this time, an offering was made to the Lord—the sacrifice of a lamb, which was slaughtered and prepared during the afternoon. Nissan 15 (the new day starting at sundown) was the beginning of the seven-day Festival of Unleavened Bread. At the start of Nissan 15, the Passover lamb was eaten, along with unleavened bread. Over time, the Festival of Unleavened Bread became more commonly known as Passover and is now usually considered to begin at sundown between Nissan 14 and Nissan 15.
